description: Common lab markers parsed through Wallach's framework. Each marker has: standard reference range, Wallach-framework interpretation (often differs from standard), corpus citations for any explicit Wallach-stated optimum, related deficiencies/conditions, and recommended-action paths. Designed for the lab_interpreter.py tool.

interpretation_legend.standard_low: below this = deficient/abnormal per standard medicine
interpretation_legend.standard_high: above this = excessive/abnormal per standard medicine
interpretation_legend.wallach_optimal_low: Wallach-framework lower bound for optimal (where corpus is explicit)
interpretation_legend.note: When Wallach's optimum differs from standard, the note explains why
interpretation_legend.deficiency_pathways: What Wallach corpus says is implicated when this marker is off

vitamin_d_25oh.name: Vitamin D, 25-hydroxy
vitamin_d_25oh.note: Modern research supports 40-60 ng/mL for mortality benefit; Wallach corpus is calcification-conservative (caps Vit D at 400 IU in cardiovascular context). Reconciliation: ensure Mg + K2 + Ca:P ratio dialed before pushing D3 high.
first_actions: If <30: Citri-D Spray (6000 IU/day) for 2-3 months then retest
If 30-40: Ultimate D3 (2500-5000 IU/day) maintenance
ALWAYS ensure Mg 400+ mg/day and K2 MK-7 100+ mcg/day cofactors
Test re-check in 8-12 weeks
products: Beyond Osteo FX (D3 + Ca + Mg + K combo)

vitamin_b12_serum.name: Vitamin B12, serum
vitamin_b12_serum.note: Wallach prefers 250-400 mcg/day supplementation (vs RDA 3-4 mcg = 80x higher). Serum >500 pg/mL strongly desirable for myelin/cognitive function per Rare Earths cobalt entry mechanism.
deficiency_pathways: demyelination of spinal cord and large nerve trunks
first_actions: If <300: methylcobalamin 1000 mcg sublingual daily; consider intrinsic-factor or H. pylori check; salt to taste (HCl support)
If 300-500: BTT 2.5 (500 mcg methylcobalamin) daily
Avoid cyanocobalamin form supplements

ferritin.name: Ferritin
ferritin.note: Ferritin is iron storage marker. Wallach corpus emphasizes iron deficiency causes (vegetarian diet, low animal protein); does NOT push high ferritin — iron at 25-50 mg/day for menstruating women, lower otherwise.
first_actions: If <50: increase red meat (Wallach: 72 oz/month), liver organ meat, iron-rich foods
Supplement iron only if dietary increase + B12/folate/Cu not enough (high iron has toxicity)
Test re-check after 3 months dietary intervention
products: Ancestral Liver (heme iron 9 mg + B12 + folate + Cu — best food-form approach)

tsh.name: TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone)
tsh.note: Wallach hypothyroid framing: 'frequently do not produce goiter, but rather produce obesity, fatigue, disinterest'. He recommends basal body temp test (below 98°F on awakening = low thyroid) as more reliable than TSH alone. Hashimoto's not in corpus.
deficiency_pathways: cobalt/B12 cofactor for thyroid hormone production
first_actions: If TSH > 2.5 with symptoms (fatigue/disinterest/cold/edema): Wallach protocol is iodine (Lugol's-equivalent) + selenium + B12
Ultimate Iodine Spray 300 mcg/day + Ultimate Selenium 3 caps (Se 300 mcg)
Pair with basal body temp monitoring (axillary temp on awakening)
Re-test in 8-12 weeks; if no improvement, consider full thyroid panel + adrenal check

free_t4.name: Free T4 (Thyroxine)
free_t4.note: T4 is thyroid hormone before conversion to active T3. Cobalt/B12 + selenium are cofactors for both production AND T4→T3 conversion.
first_actions: Same as TSH — iodine + selenium + B12 stack

free_t3.name: Free T3 (Triiodothyronine, active)
free_t3.note: T3 is the active thyroid hormone. Low T3 with normal T4 = conversion problem (selenium/zinc dependent).
first_actions: Selenium 300+ mcg/day selenomethionine + Zn 15-30 mg/day

homocysteine.name: Homocysteine
homocysteine.note: Elevated homocysteine = methylation cofactor deficiency (B6, B12, folate). Cardiovascular risk marker. Modern marker (not Wallach-named) but mechanistically aligned with his B-complex emphasis.
first_actions: If >10: methylcobalamin B12 + methylfolate (5-MTHF) + P5P (active B6)
BTT 2.5 has all three active forms (methylcobalamin 500 mcg, methylfolate 400 mcg, but standard B6)
Ultimate Cardio FX has P5P (8 mg) + methylcobalamin 100 mcg + methylfolate 1360 mcg DFE

total_cholesterol.name: Total Cholesterol
total_cholesterol.note: **KEY FRAMEWORK CONFLICT.** Standard medicine pushes total cholesterol <200 via statins. Wallach explicitly recommends MAINTAINING cholesterol via daily eggs + 72 oz red meat/month to rebuild myelin. He treats elevated cholesterol with niacin + Cr + fiber + EFAs — NOT statins. Statins simultaneously deplete CoQ10 and block endogenous cholesterol myelin substrate.
deficiency_pathways: if LOW: dietary cholesterol restriction, statin use, low animal protein → cognitive decline risk
if HIGH: insulin resistance, Cr deficiency, low-fiber diet
first_actions: If <180: increase dietary cholesterol (eggs daily, red meat), confirm B12 status for myelin synthesis
If 180-240: optimal range; check HDL/LDL/triglyceride ratio
If >240: Wallach protocol = niacin 450 mg b.i.d. time-release + Cr 75 mcg t.i.d. + Se 100 mcg t.i.d. + EFAs 5g t.i.d. + fiber (oat bran 1-2 tbsp/day); not statins
products: Ultimate Cardio FX (P5P + active B forms + 690 mg cardio blend)

ldl_cholesterol.name: LDL Cholesterol
ldl_cholesterol.note: Standard target <100 (or <70 with CV history). Wallach corpus does not target LDL specifically; treats elevated total cholesterol via lifestyle/supplement protocol. LDL particle size matters more than total (modern paradigm extension).
deficiency_pathways: if very LOW: same myelin concern as low total cholesterol
first_actions: See total cholesterol; lifestyle + Wallach protocol over statins

hdl_cholesterol.name: HDL Cholesterol
hdl_cholesterol.note: Higher HDL = better. Niacin and EFAs raise HDL.
deficiency_pathways: low HDL: insulin resistance, sedentary, low EFAs
first_actions: Niacin (Ultimate Niacin Plus 500 mg time-release), EFAs (EFA Plus 5g)
Exercise

triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
triglycerides.note: Triglyceride/HDL ratio is the best CV risk single marker (modern; ratio <2 ideal). High triglycerides = high carb/sugar intake. Wallach-aligned: reduce sugar, increase Cr + EFAs.
first_actions: Reduce sugar/refined carbs
Cr GTF-aligned + EFAs
Re-test in 8-12 weeks

fasting_glucose.name: Fasting Glucose
fasting_glucose.note: Wallach's blood sugar framework is Cr + V driven. 6-hour GTT (glucose tolerance test) is his preferred diagnostic for both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia.
deficiency_pathways: chromium deficiency (300% higher Cr loss with sugar intake)
first_actions: If 90-99 (pre-diabetic range): Cr nicotinate glycinate + V at Wallach diabetes protocol dose (Cr 250 mcg, V 250 mcg)
If <70: hypoglycemia protocol (Cr + V + Mg + B-complex)
6-hour GTT recommended

hba1c.name: Hemoglobin A1c
hba1c.note: 3-month average blood sugar. Wallach's diabetes protocol (Cr + V) targets reducing this gradually.
first_actions: Same as fasting glucose; Cr+V GTF-aligned protocol

testosterone_total.name: Testosterone, Total
testosterone_total.note: Wallach's T-axis lever is boron (doubles T per Rare Earths/DDDL). For lab-confirmed low T: Zn 50 mg t.i.d. protocol per testicular atrophy entry. See why-layer-hormones-strength.md.
first_actions: If <400 (low T direction): XeraTest (boron 3 mg + Zn 30 mg) + Ultimate Selenium 3 caps + Ancestral Liver 6 caps (Cu rebalance)
If <300 (clinical low T): escalate Zn toward 50 mg t.i.d. (150 mg/day) protocol with Ultimate Zinc stacking; ensure Cu 4-6 mg/day
Maintain salt to taste; daily eggs + red meat for cholesterol → hormone synthesis
products: Beyond Osteo FX Liquid (Boron 3 mg + bone cluster)

testosterone_free.name: Testosterone, Free
testosterone_free.note: Free T is the bioactive fraction. Low free T with normal total T = SHBG too high (often from low animal protein or high estrogen).
deficiency_pathways: same as total T, plus SHBG-driving factors
first_actions: Same as total T plus increase animal protein

shbg.name: SHBG (Sex Hormone Binding Globulin)
shbg.note: Binds T, making it bioinactive. Low animal protein + high estrogen + thyroid issues raise SHBG.
first_actions: Increase animal protein (Wallach: 120 g/day)
Optimize thyroid axis

estradiol_e2_male.name: Estradiol (E2) - Male
estradiol_e2_male.note: **FRAMEWORK CAVEAT.** Wallach's boron mechanism doubles BOTH T and E. If supplementing boron and E2 trends high, modern aromatase-management (DIM) is framework-adjacent, not Wallach-named.
deficiency_pathways: if high: aromatase activity, alcohol, body fat
if low: dietary fat, healthy cholesterol synthesis
first_actions: If E2 >40 on boron supplementation: consider DIM 200 mg/day (modern), reduce alcohol, reduce body fat
products: see hormones WHY-layer for full context

dhea_s.name: DHEA-Sulfate
dhea_s.note: Adrenal output marker. Falls with age. Modern paradigm supplements DHEA directly; Wallach corpus largely silent.
first_actions: Ultimate D-Stress (adrenal support: B1 50 + B5 1000 + adrenal substance)
If labs confirm low, modern DHEA 25 mg/day
products: Ultimate Hormone FX (DHEA 25 mg — women's product)

cortisol_am.name: Cortisol, AM (8am)
cortisol_am.note: Morning cortisol. Too high = chronic stress; too low = adrenal fatigue. Caffeine raises cortisol acutely (modern endocrinology, not Wallach-named).
first_actions: B5 (pantothenic acid) 1g+ via Ultimate D-Stress; reduce caffeine; ashwagandha (modern adaptogen)

ferritin_zn_cu.name: Zinc / Copper / Selenium serum panel
ferritin_zn_cu.note: Standard medicine rarely tests trace mineral status. Hair analysis (Wallach-recommended) is the preferred Wallach diagnostic. Modern serum Zn (60-120 mcg/dL), Cu (70-140 mcg/dL), Se (70-150 mcg/L) are crude.
ferritin_zn_cu.wallach_optimal: Hair analysis recommended — see why-layer-hormones-strength.md for protocol-dose stacking
first_actions: Hair analysis via Doctor's Data Labs or similar; serum Zn/Cu/Se as floor check

vitamin_a_serum.name: Vitamin A (Retinol), serum
vitamin_a_serum.note: Beta-carotene preferred over retinol for high-dose supplementation (Wallach's preference). Conversion to retinol is liver-regulated, safer than retinol toxicity at high dose.
first_actions: Beta-carotene 25,000-300,000 IU/day per protocol; food sources (liver, eggs, orange vegetables)

vitamin_e_serum.name: Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol), serum
vitamin_e_serum.note: Wallach's cardiovascular dose is 800-1200 IU/day; cataracts and macular degeneration use 1200-2000 IU/day. Succinate form preferred.
first_actions: ReVERSE!® (134 mg d-alpha tocopheryl succinate + mixed tocopherols + tocotrienols)
Integris CoQ10+Vit E Succinate (66 mg)

iodine_urine.name: Iodine, urinary spot (Iodine Loading Test)
iodine_urine.note: Wallach recommends iodine more aggressively than standard medicine (Lugol's-style). Modern functional medicine pushes 150-300 mcg/L. Test via 24-hour collection or iodine loading test (Optimox).
first_actions: Ultimate Iodine Spray 300 mcg/day; Ocean's Gold 500 mcg/day for higher dose

selenium_serum.name: Selenium, serum
selenium_serum.note: Wallach's Se dose is 200-1000 mcg/day across protocols (cancer prevention, eye disease, thyroid). Serum levels often run low in US populations due to soil depletion.
first_actions: Ultimate Selenium 3 caps/day (Se 300 mcg L-selenomethionine)

magnesium_rbc.name: Magnesium, RBC (red blood cell)
magnesium_rbc.note: RBC Mg is more sensitive than serum Mg. Wallach's protocol dose is 1000 mg/day across most conditions.
first_actions: Cal Toddy Liquid (600 mg Mg citrate)
Beyond Osteo FX (300 mg Mg)
Mg glycinate 400-800 mg/day if RBC <5.5

crp_hs.name: C-Reactive Protein, high-sensitivity
crp_hs.note: Inflammation marker. Modern marker (not Wallach-named). High CRP = systemic inflammation → cardiovascular, cancer, autoimmune risk.
first_actions: Ultimate EFA Plus 6/day; antioxidant load (Cell Shield RTQ); pulse test for food allergens

uric_acid.name: Uric Acid
uric_acid.note: Gout marker. Wallach gout protocol = baseline supplements + folic acid + cherry juice + reduce purine-heavy foods. Modern paradigm: also indicates oxidative stress.
first_actions: Cherry juice/extract; folic acid 5-10 mg/day; reduce alcohol; hydration
